questions.stem: Which statement is true for every integer n?
choices: If n is positive, n − 1 is positive.
If n is even, n/2 is odd.
If n is negative, n² is negative.
If n is odd, n + 1 is even.

guide.explanation: An odd integer has form 2k + 1, so adding 1 gives 2(k + 1), which is even. Counterexamples for the others are n = 4, 1, and −1.
guide.shortcut: Check whether the claim is always true; a single counterexample defeats an always claim.
